question.problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given in the table below. Find $\text{E}[Y\sqrt{X}].$

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.1$ | $0.5$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.2$ | $0.2$ |
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables with supports ${S}_{X}$ and ${S}_{Y},$ respectively, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability mass function with support $S={S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y}.$ If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}r(x,y)\,f(x,y).
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)=y\sqrt{x}.
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y\sqrt{X}] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}r(x,y)\,f(x,y) \\  & =(1\cdot \sqrt{1})\cdot f(1,1)+(2\cdot \sqrt{1})\cdot f(1,2)+(1\cdot \sqrt{4})\cdot f(4,1)+(2\cdot \sqrt{4})\cdot f(4,2) \\  & =1\cdot f(1,1)+2\cdot f(1,2)+2\cdot f(4,1)+4\cdot f(4,2) \\  & =1\cdot 0.1+2\cdot 0.5+2\cdot 0.2+4\cdot 0.2 \\  & =0.1+1+0.4+0.8 \\  & =2.3.\end{aligned}
$$
